title: Client-side idle probing, pool sharding, and adaptive keepalive presets for cross-language SDKs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers running long-lived connections from browser/edge services and backend workers experience either unnecessary reconnect churn or idle socket bloat. We need cross-SDK guidance and runtime defaults that strike the right balance: minimize cold-starts and TCP handshakes, prevent file-descriptor exhaustion in highly concurrent clients, and surface ergonomics for streaming APIs so users can tune behavior without brittle low-level configs.

Goal: Ship a cross-language set of adaptive defaults and example presets for: connection pooling size, per-route idle-probing (TCP keepalive and application PING), pool sharding by route and auth token, proactive socket reaping policy, and quick-to-use high/low-latency presets. Provide idiomatic examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, plus a migration guide for existing customers.

Scope:
- SDK defaults and public config schema (all three languages).
- Helper utilities: pool-sharder, idle-probe manager, and diagnostic hooks.
- Telemetry: per-connection lifecycle metrics, socket_reuse_ratio, pool_spill_events, and probe_latency_histogram.
- Integration tests and perf benchmarks under mixed latency workloads.

Out of scope for this ticket: server-side runtime changes, Dedicated autoscaling knobs, and on-prem packaging improvements. Those will be follow-ups if telemetry indicates server-side hotspots.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-SDK config object defined and documented with 3 example presets: default, low-latency, cost-optimized
Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs include helper API to create sharded pools with per-route keys
E2E perf test shows >=20% reduction in average cold-connection handshakes for bursty traffic in default preset
Telemetry emits socket_reuse_ratio and pool_spill_events for every host/route within 2 weeks of rollout
Docs and migration guide published in DevPortal with code snippets and rollback guidance
design_decisions: Use application-level sharding key composed of (route, auth_hash_prefix) rather than sharding by CPU/core; simpler to reason across languages
Default pool size = max(2, min(concurrency_hint, 16)) with LRU eviction for least-recently-used route pools
Idle probing combines OS TCP keepalive (if supported) + lightweight application PING; allow disabling app-PING for environments where probes are expensive
Expose adaptive_idle_timeout which shortens with high connection pressure and extends when reuse is frequent
Expose a single high-level config object (TransportConfig) across SDKs; runtime maps it to native HTTP/Socket options
rollout_plan: Feature branch with transport shim and defaults merged behind feature flag 'shim.transport_v2'
Canary SDK release to 5 internal teams with telemetry enabled (1 week)
Gradual public rollout: opt-in beta via environment variable for 2 weeks, then default on for new installs
Monitor pool_spill_events, socket_reuse_ratio, and SLO telemetry during each phase; rollback on >5% increase in 5xx attributable to connection churn
telemetry: add tags: sdk_lang, route, region, auth_tier
tests: unit: verify sharder maps keys to deterministic shards and evicts correctly
integration: emulator tests that simulate 10k short-lived connections with mixed auth tokens
perf: benchmark cold-start handshake reduction compared to v1 defaults under bursty traffic
stability: soak test for 72 hours with high concurrency to check FD leakage
